Question: Can the platform generate realistic synthetic datasets for testing agent behaviour, edge cases, and failure modes; respecting privacy and bias considerations?
Response: Yes. Foundry provides synthetic data generation capabilities for testing agentic workflows. For POC2: 500 synthetic CVs generated for bias/accuracy testing of the screening skill, driven through the full MAF workflow graph (screening agent executor + bias-marker validator executor). An agent executor can itself generate synthetic test data via the code interpreter sandbox — producing realistic datasets following specified distributions, demographics and edge cases. Privacy: synthetic data has no PII linkage to real individuals. Bias testing: evaluation runs compare screening outcomes across demographic dimensions to detect and measure bias. Generation parameters configurable and auditable.
Key Technologies: Foundry synthetic data, GHCP SDK code interpreter, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 workflow graph, Foundry Evaluators
POC Demo: POC2: Generate 500 synthetic CVs, run screening skill against them, evaluate for bias and accuracy with Foundry Evaluators.

Question: Describe evaluator agents that systematically test responses across prompt variations, adversarial inputs, and regression suites.
Response: Foundry Evaluators provide systematic evaluation across multiple dimensions: task adherence, tool call accuracy, safety, groundedness and sensitive data exposure. Evaluations run end-to-end through the MAF workflow graph so that agent executors, validator executors and the conditional edges between them are all exercised. (1) Prompt variation testing — run the same task with different skill configurations and prompt variations, compare quality metrics. (2) Adversarial testing — adversarial input generation for prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, edge case inputs; MAF validator executors act as a structural defence and are tested for their catch rate. (3) Regression suites — defined evaluation datasets with expected outcomes, run in APIOps CI/CD before skill promotion. Results feed the API Center lifecycle: a skill (or a graph-level change that swaps an agent executor for a plain-function executor) cannot be promoted to Production if evaluation scores fall below thresholds. Fleet Manager runs continuous evaluation on production traffic.
Key Technologies: Foundry Evaluators, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 (validators as structural defence tested by evaluations), API Center lifecycle gates, Fleet Manager continuous evaluation, APIOps CI/CD integration
POC Demo: POC2: Show multi-prompt evaluation of screening skill — variation testing across prompt configurations with quality comparison dashboard.

Question: Describe ongoing monitoring of agent performance against baselines with automated alerts when quality, accuracy, or behaviour drifts beyond thresholds.
Response: Multi-layer drift detection. (1) Foundry Evaluators: continuous evaluation on production traffic. Task Adherence evaluator detects drift from defined purpose. Quality scores tracked against baselines; alerts when scores drop below thresholds. (2) MAF validator executors: produce per-workflow pass/fail signals that are themselves a drift indicator — rising validator failure rate on an agent executor output indicates the agent is drifting before downstream quality is affected. (3) APIM AI Gateway: per-model, per-agent metrics (latency, error rate, token usage, cost); statistical anomaly detection. (4) Fleet Manager agent: reasons about fleet-wide quality trends, consuming Foundry Evaluator output, MAF validator results and APIM metrics. Detects emerging patterns (e.g. screening accuracy declining for a specific job category) and surfaces proactive alerts with recommended actions (investigate, revert skill version, increase HITL oversight). Alerts flow through Azure Monitor.
Key Technologies: Foundry Evaluators (continuous), Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) validator executors (drift signal), APIM anomaly detection, Fleet Manager trend analysis, Azure Monitor alerts
POC Demo: POC2: Show drift detection — screening accuracy drops for engineering roles, Fleet Manager alerts HR BP with root cause analysis and recommendations.

Question: Do you provide sandboxed simulation environments where agents can be tested against realistic scenarios at scale before production deployment?
Response: Yes. The dev/staging/production lifecycle provides sandboxed environments at each stage. Staging: full simulation with mock APIs (WPP sandbox APIs for Workday, D365, Greenhouse) running real MAF workflow graphs end-to-end — DF envelopes coordinating phases, agent executors invoking GHCP SDK sessions, validator executors enforcing constraints. Foundry supports separate projects per environment with isolated configurations. API Center lifecycle gates ensure skills and graph-level changes are tested in staging before production promotion. For scale simulation: DF can run hundreds of concurrent simulated workflows; MAF graphs fan out via Pregel BSP. Synthetic data generation (500 CVs, synthetic invoices) provides realistic test data. Foundry Evaluators run comprehensive suites. Staging mirrors production configuration (APIM policies, Foundry Guardrails, skill versions, MAF graph definitions) with sandbox integrations.
Key Technologies: Foundry staging projects, API Center lifecycle, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0, MAF Durable Task extension, Azure Durable Functions (scale simulation), sandbox APIs
POC Demo: POC2: Show staging environment with 500 synthetic CVs processed through the full screening pipeline, evaluated for quality before production deployment.
